question: A support team and a marketing team share one project. Support wants terse troubleshooting answers; marketing wants warm promotional copy. The project owner wants consistent quality for both. What should the owner do first?
options: A) Keep one project and ask each person to restate their preferred tone at the start of every chat.
B) Split the work into two projects, each with instructions written for that team's audience and purpose.
C) Ask Claude to work out from each question whether the person is in support or marketing, and adapt.
D) Write one set of instructions listing both styles and let each person say which one they want in each chat.
correct_answers: B) Split the work into two projects, each with instructions written for that team's audience and purpose.
explanations: This abandons durable direction entirely and reintroduces the inconsistency being complained about.
Correct. Durable direction only works when one workspace serves one audience and purpose.
Guessing the requester's team from the wording is unreliable and leaves no explicit standard.
This is a conflicting rule set that pushes the choice back into every individual conversation.
